questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic challenges and a thriving professional environment in my field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to navigate my different courses, both in terms of where they were located on campus, and whether I could change courses. I ended up taking a different class than I wanted - simply because I couldn't find classroom, contact information of the professor or anybody to ask.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received friendly, but not very helpful assistance. It seemed as if nobody was exactly sure who should help me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, but Bikubenfonden is my greatest recommendation to any incoming students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Unless you get Bikubenfonden's Academic Guest House, any room will be expensive. Like 2.000 dollars a month in 2026. But I would look in Brooklyn, Greenpoint, and Bushwick, if I was to look at housing outside Manhattan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was just next to no housing available on campus for exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: If I understand the question correctly, I needed to browse their catalog of courses, choose and apply for the relevant ones, purchase a health insurance through NYU, upload proof of medical records (which my doctor back home should approve), and apply for a visa.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NYU did a good job of sending me emails explaining the different steps and overall had a high level of communication.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I got them all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Begin with plenty of time to spare.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was high, as most MA-courses consisted of an equal amount of phd and master's students. They pushed me to become better.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All my classes in the literature-department were seminars, which meant small classrooms of 5-7 students and 1-2 professors and discussion based teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Declaring Independence: Politics, Aesthetics and Ethics. 
2. Strange Connections: Translational Poetics.
3. Africa in Theory.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Declaring Independence: Politics, Aesthetics and Ethics. 
We looked at major works throughout the American literary history to trace the development of 'freedom' as a concept.

questions.answer: Language test, visa application and application to NYU were about 3500 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Health insurance was by far the most expensive part of my trip.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Any really, and NYU were amazing at advertising them. I'm pretty sure it would be possible to have your entire social battery filled up just by their clubs and gatherings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined both a French speaking-club off campus (found through Facebook) and the church Redeemer West Side. Both were great!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Washington DC, Boston and if you have the time: Buy a 10-trip pass to Amtrak (their train system), so you can take both shorter and longer trips. I went to San Fransisco which was just amazing!
In New York I would recommend the tram to Roosevelt Island, the South Ferry that goes past the Statue of Liberty, 9/11 Memorial, MoMA, The Met and go see a Yankees game.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: New York has almost any subculture. So seek out yours and find locals who enjoy the same hobby. Facebook is often a good place to start and search for events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it tricky to figure out when I could count on people. As the pace of the city is so high, many are friendly and open, but friendships doesn't have a high level of commitment. So it took me a while before I found 'my people'.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their expressiveness. Americans are open and typically speak their mind. It made it quite easy to talk to new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to seek community outside of the classes as well (it's not always the easiest thing to find community in just two hours' seminars every week). 
Use the city. NYU has a million different clubs, special deals on Broadway and trips that you can browse from. 
Be ready to do the work.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Engage with the professors and use their office hours.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To have small classes of just five students and two professors. I learned so much!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: New York City. The paste was exhausting some days, and I found myself tired to a completely different level (even though the city was also exciting and amazing). New York is a lot of things, but boring is not one of them.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
